355.title: Dispel level-three-or-lower spells on one explicit creature
355.body:
<!-- edda-271:dispel-low -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 124, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

An isolated authorized level-five Cleric fixture uses level-three Dispel Magic on a known creature carrying Shield of Faith and Bless from independent casters.

## Targets

One known creature within 120 feet and clear path; end every qualifying ongoing spell on that target. A multi-recipient cast loses only the targeted recipient link, not other recipients.

## Costs

Magic action, one level-three slot, V/S. Automatic ending for ongoing spells level three or lower; no ability check for these spells.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Commit action cost, exact affected spell/link IDs and history together. Distinguish ending the target’s spell effect from ending its caster’s unrelated concentration.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `spell.dispel.creature.low-level`, `effect.remove.recipient-link`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test several qualifying spells, suppressed same-name effects, unrelated targets/casters, no eligible spells (legal cast still costs), reload and exact removal once.
- [ ] Reject unknown spell levels, level-four-or-higher effects and object/magical-effect targets with an explicit unsupported reason until the bounded follow-up decides them. Isolated authorized fixture only; production eligibility requires exact #323 advancement child, not decision closure.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #203
- #352

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No general antimagic, curses, nonspell magic-item removal, object/area targeting, higher-level checks/upcasting or automatic class advancement. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

356.title: Persist one Counterspell reaction window around Cure Wounds casting
356.body:
<!-- edda-271:counterspell-window -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 120, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

A prepared Cleric attempts the existing level-one Cure Wounds self cast while one explicitly known authorized NPC Counterspell caster has a reaction and level-three slot.

## Targets

One visible known casting creature within 60 feet, with V/S/M casting observable and clear path. Use an isolated trusted NPC fixture, not a general monster caster entitlement.

## Costs

Counterspell: one Reaction, one level-three slot, S. Target Constitution save against reactor’s spell DC. Failure wastes target’s casting action/Bonus Action/Reaction but does not expend its spell slot; success permits original cast once.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Suspend before original spell resolves or spends its slot; persist casting attempt and trigger identity plus actor’s spent casting time. Explicit react/decline and stale confirmation. Concentration replacement starts when casting starts, even if interrupted.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `casting.pending-attempt`, `reaction.counterspell.constitution`, `casting.countered.slot-not-spent`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test failed and successful saves, decline, unavailable reaction, no components, unseen/foreign/out-of-range trigger, stale pending attempt, crash/reconnect before and after decision and duplicate confirmation.
- [ ] Persist original attempt, reaction cost, save and resume/cancel outcome atomically. If the target fails its Constitution save, the interrupted spell never heals and never spends the target slot; if the target succeeds, the original spell resolves and heals once. Existing opportunity-reaction flow remains bounded and intact.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.

- #201

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No 2014 ability-check or automatic-level Counterspell, nested counter-counterspell, multiplayer priority, item/free-use refunds, new NPC spell AI, general Wizard builds or player discovery. 430.title: Confirm creation proficiency provenance for Barbarian consumers
430.body:
<!-- edda-321:origin-provenance -->
Parent: #333; decision #321; roadmap #47; blocks #498; #498 directly blocks #337.

Delivery: one reviewable PR, Task Size M.

Source: pinned English SRD5.2.1 pp28-30 and explicitly named referenced pages below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md.

Scope and deterministic positive fixture: PDF pp19-23/28: preserve selected species/background ability/skill/tool/language/feat provenance separately from class grants; reject duplicate class-skill selections and unsupported origins. Resolve duplicate proficiency choices by their source rules; no silent replacements or doubled PB. Preview the complete creation combination; this PR implements provenance validation only, no new species or feat effects.

Negative fixtures: violate each stated eligibility/number/target/action/resource/timing predicate independently; reject unsupported variants and forged levels. Preview and cancellation never mutate.

Required acceptance: Authoritative campaign/actor/source/rules-version/class-level eligibility; isolated high-level test entitlements grant no production access. Prepare previews costs/choices/targets/timing without dice or writes; explicit confirm revalidates current revision and commits choices, injectable dice, resource/action costs, effects, derived sheet and public history atomically. Store durable action receipt: same-ID retry/reload/reconnect returns exact committed result with no reroll/recharge/regrant; conflicting payload or concurrent stale confirmation rejected; two concurrent confirmations spend/apply once. Inject history/effect/choice failure and prove full PostgreSQL rollback. Protect private NPC HP, hidden actors, tactics and private choices in discovery/preview/history/error/reconnect. Shared web/TUI availability, disabled reason, accessible confirmation/cancel and reconnect fixtures required; desktop/phone confirmation journeys for changed web UI. Unknown prerequisites fail closed. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL integration rollback/replay/reload/concurrency tests; frontend build, changed-file lint and behavior fixtures when UI changes. Preserve legacy reads/unrelated JSON; retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptations. No production deployment, inference or broad coverage promotion.

Ownership: feature resolvers own behavior; level/entry applications consume them and apply grants once. Feature tests use explicit isolated entitlements, never grant production class admission. Data and earlier levels never unlock broader support. Shared #272 rests, #273 casting, #333 origins, #335 multiclass, #336 advancement, #384 selection/#389 ability updater, #269/#270 conditions and #278 equipment retain their scopes. Exact shared terminals in this matrix must block #498 natively; #498 blocks #337. Planning closure is insufficient. Selected feat effect must have its own terminal gate before admission; never implement spell/item effects here. No child implementation or qualification is supplied by this decision.

502.title: Route Bard slot casts and instrument focus through authoritative receipts
502.body:
<!-- edda-322:casting-route -->
Parent: #193; decision #322; roadmap #47. Task Size M.

One reviewable PR. Required path: this terminal -> Bard gate #501 -> #337. Additional direct qualification gates: [279, 280].

Source: pinned English SRD5.2.1 PDF31-35; exact referenced pages in scope below. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. Attribution/license/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; CC-BY-4.0. Source facts paraphrased; fixture/ownership choices are Edda additions.

Scope: PDF104-106: eligible prepared Bard spell, CHA attack/DC (PB+CHA / 8+PB+CHA), slot level >= spell level, exact action/components and one slot spent to cast per turn. Musical Instrument focus substitutes only noncostly nonconsumed material with hand availability; require armor training. Preserve independent source-linked slot/free-use identity for Magic Initiate #386. Do not grant free Bard casts, rituals, costly-material bypass or spell effects. Consume #68/#273 casting receipt contract.

Positive deterministic fixture: Prepared Cure Wounds uses one level1 slot and instrument when eligible; same receipt on retry.

Negative deterministic fixture: Reject unprepared spell, wrong source/list, missing V/S/hand, untrained armor, costly/consumed substitution, insufficient slot or second slot-cast.

Required acceptance: For this one PR, preview is inert; explicit confirmation revalidates authoritative eligibility, source/version, target facts and expected revision. Persist choice, exact dice, once-only cost/use and history atomically. Receipt replay/retry/reload returns the same result without rerolling or charging again. Inject history failure for full rollback; race two confirmations and require one commit; stale/foreign/unsupported state rejects without mutation. Prove this with deterministic dice and isolated PostgreSQL handler/state fixtures. Disclose only player-known targets, choices, costs and source derivations; hidden/foreign facts never enter previews, receipts or errors. Shared engine serves web and TUI: explicitly expose supported choices or show unavailable with a reason on both; require desktop/phone confirmation and reconnect plus TUI behavior fixtures before availability. No Full Rules/coverage promotion. Higher-level isolated fixture state never grants production entitlement. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p 2 ./...; changed UI requires build, focused lint and behavior tests.

Feature tests use explicit isolated entitlements, never production grants. Transitions consume exact implemented contracts and apply grants once. Unknown options/effects/origins/multiclass configurations fail closed. #272/#427/#428 own completed rests; #273 casting modes, #58 sheet projection, #333/#430 proficiency provenance, #336/#429 advancement transaction, #335 multiclass contracts, #384 selection/#389 caps. #277 spells/#278 items/#269/#270 conditions retain shared effects. Chosen feat/spell effects require their exact terminal and qualification path before availability; source import or planning closure never supplies execution. No runtime/grants/coverage promotion or deployment in this decision.

Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

Level 2 Conjuration (Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 60 feet
Components: V, S, M (a bit of spiderweb)
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour
You conjure a mass of sticky webbing at a point
within range. The webs fill a 20-foot Cube there for
the duration. The webs are Difficult Terrain, and the
area within them is Lightly Obscured.
If the webs aren’t anchored between two solid
masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across
a floor, wall, or ceiling, the web collapses on itself,
and the spell ends at the start of your next turn.
Webs layered over a flat surface have a depth of 5
feet.
The first time a creature enters the webs on a
turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a
Dexterity saving throw or have the Restrained con-
dition while in the webs or until it breaks free.
A creature Restrained by the webs can take an
action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against
your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer
Restrained.
The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot Cube of webs
exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing 2d4
Fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in
the fire.

Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

<!-- roadmap-slicer:edda-story-led-srd-521:issue:spell-items-casting-modes -->

Epic: #193 · Parent coverage: #54 · Roadmap: #47 · Decision: #80

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1, PDF pp. 104–107](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf). Pin, license and attribution: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`. Decision/inventory: `docs/investigations/issue-80-spell-item-expansion.md` and `issue-80-spell-item-inventory.json`.

**Spike: one working session; one decision PR plus published bounded follow-ups.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inspect only these named scopes: ritual casting; costly materials; consumed materials; spell scroll casting; item spells/concentration; slot/free-use routing. Record exact source rules, existing evidence and unknowns; do not guess production mechanics.
- [ ] Publish one-PR implementation children with a named fixture, source pages, targets/costs/timing, durable/replay/disclosure tests, exclusions and hard prerequisites. Keep wider scope as explicitly named bounded spikes.
- [ ] Attach children under this tracking group and add exact implementation blockers to full spell/item qualification before closing. Decision closure is not implementation evidence; read back every child, parent and blocking edge.

## Blocked by

- #80

## Verification

- `go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`.
- For mutations: isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests with injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload.
- For UI: frontend build, changed-file lint, behavior fixtures and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys.
- Data-only work: offline source/schema/name/variant fixtures, no inference or production data.
- Spikes: publish/read back child issues, native hierarchy and exact blocking edges to the qualification gates before closing.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler/character UI fixtures. Preserve legacy reads and the shared web/TUI engine. Unknown mechanics remain unavailable. No adjacent batches, production mutation, hidden-lore disclosure or unsupported Full Rules claims. Source-derived data retains CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptation notices. Close work from its merged PR.

351.title: Track two Shield of Faith casters with independent recipient effects
351.body:
<!-- edda-271:effect-identity -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 162, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

Two explicitly prepared level-one Clerics cast Shield of Faith at separate times on one known creature within 60 feet, then one caster ends concentration.

## Targets

One known same-campaign creature per cast; retain the existing conscious-self path. Require authoritative range and clear path; reject unknown range, total cover, foreign or hidden recipients.

## Costs

Each cast: one level-one slot, Bonus Action, V/S and noncostly material/focus availability; one-slot-per-turn limit. Voluntary ending: no action or slot refund.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Absolute start/expiry seconds, maximum 600 seconds. Replace only the casting caster’s previous concentration. Equal-potency overlapping +2 AC applies once, latest casting active; ending it reveals an older still-live effect without restarting its clock.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `effect.instance.caster-recipient`, `effect.same-spell.latest-equal`, `effect.duration.absolute`, `concentration.owner`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

- [ ] Persist cast identity separately from recipient links; remove all links only for the ended cast. Different casters never overwrite each other. Preserve old self-only saves and unrelated stats.

Authoritative preview is inert: no writes/dice; explicit confirm revalidates actor/campaign/source/class level/expected revision, targets, range, action, resource and costs. Durable receipt binds payload: retry/replay/reload/reconnect returns exact result; conflicting payload and stale state reject. Concurrent confirmations commit once. Inject cost/effect/history failures and prove complete isolated PostgreSQL rollback. Web AND trusted TUI expose availability/reasons, accessible confirmation/cancel/reconnect; changed web requires desktop/phone journeys, build and focused lint. For passive/source-automatic effects confirmation belongs to triggering action/turn, never invent optional activation. Unknown facts remain unavailable; no hidden target/HP/DC disclosure. Source catalogues do not unlock actions. Consume qualified named terminals; never copy spell/item/condition effects or another class eligibility. Unknown authoritative world/possession/plane/item facts stay unavailable. For automatic benefits,use triggering confirmed event; no invented optional activation.

Dispel Magic.title: Dispel level-three-or-lower spells on one explicit creature
Dispel Magic.body:
<!-- edda-271:dispel-low -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 124, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

An isolated authorized level-five Cleric fixture uses level-three Dispel Magic on a known creature carrying Shield of Faith and Bless from independent casters.

## Targets

One known creature within 120 feet and clear path; end every qualifying ongoing spell on that target. A multi-recipient cast loses only the targeted recipient link, not other recipients.

## Costs

Magic action, one level-three slot, V/S. Automatic ending for ongoing spells level three or lower; no ability check for these spells.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Commit action cost, exact affected spell/link IDs and history together. Distinguish ending the target’s spell effect from ending its caster’s unrelated concentration.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `spell.dispel.creature.low-level`, `effect.remove.recipient-link`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test several qualifying spells, suppressed same-name effects, unrelated targets/casters, no eligible spells (legal cast still costs), reload and exact removal once.
- [ ] Reject unknown spell levels, level-four-or-higher effects and object/magical-effect targets with an explicit unsupported reason until the bounded follow-up decides them. Isolated authorized fixture only; production eligibility requires exact #323 advancement child, not decision closure.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #203
- #352

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No general antimagic, curses, nonspell magic-item removal, object/area targeting, higher-level checks/upcasting or automatic class advancement. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

ceed on a Wisdom saving throw or shape-shift into

Beast you choose that has a Challenge Rating equal
to or less than the target’s (or the target’s level if
it doesn’t have a Challenge Rating). The target’s
game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the
chosen Beast, but the target retains its alignment,
personality, creature type, Hit Points, and Hit Point
Dice. See the “Animals” section of “Monsters” for a
sample of Beast stat blocks.
The target gains a number of Temporary Hit
Points equal to the Hit Points of the Beast form.
These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain
when the spell ends. The spell ends early on the tar-
get if it has no Temporary Hit Points left.
The target is limited in the actions it can perform
by the anatomy of its new form, and it can’t speak or
cast spells.
The target’s gear melds into the new form. The
creature can’t use or otherwise benefit from any of
that equipment.

Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

Level 2 Conjuration (Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 60 feet
Components: V, S, M (a bit of spiderweb)
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour
You conjure a mass of sticky webbing at a point
within range. The webs fill a 20-foot Cube there for
the duration. The webs are Difficult Terrain, and the
area within them is Lightly Obscured.
If the webs aren’t anchored between two solid
masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across
a floor, wall, or ceiling, the web collapses on itself,
and the spell ends at the start of your next turn.
Webs layered over a flat surface have a depth of 5
feet.
The first time a creature enters the webs on a
turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a
Dexterity saving throw or have the Restrained con-
dition while in the webs or until it breaks free.
A creature Restrained by the webs can take an
action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against
your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer
Restrained.
The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot Cube of webs
exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing 2d4
Fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in
the fire.
